entity_policy: SOURCE entities only. Window entities are the windows themselves: a seeded share (about 30-90%, rising after each shift) are 'living' windows with raised blinds over a dim room, where shadowy silhouettes flit at the edge of vision; looking straight at one hurts. A pink-dress faceling keeps to one corridor floor and is lethal at arm's length (log 4). Silhouettes appear at corridor corners and vanish when looked at or approached. Skin-stealers are named by the page but given no description or behaviour, so none is spawned. No settlement, no NPC.
notes: SOURCE: irregular indoor atrium about 45 m across and 30 m tall; stark white concrete walls with windows at even intervals, roughly 100-200 at a time, most with blinds; a quarter to almost all replaced by living window entities; pentagonal path with four perpendicular inroads to a hollow pale birchwood circle that cannot be pried open; living moss between the paths; a table, gramophone, photographs, books, vases and an alarm clock placed arbitrarily; cold (13.8 C), dry, silent; avoid windows other than the entry, glass railings, the circle, the table and its objects; emergency protocol of covering eyes and ears and staying still for 6-8 hours; mahogany doors that appear and shift, leading to white, harshly lit corridors on several floors with stairwells and walkways above the atrium; most doors locked from the inside, the open rooms blank white squares; facelings and silhouettes in the halls; the entry window disappears within 2-3 minutes; vacant windows rumoured to lead to Level 1.5; logs: clock in the centre, table in the far corner, the table later in the middle, windows shifted and multiplied, gramophone playing, balloons on the floor. ADAPTATION: (1) the polygon, window size, 4 m row pitch and the exact spacing (seeded 5.2-6.4 m, tightening after each shift; a seventh row appears) are ours within the page's figures; (2) the exposure meter and its rates, the death texts, and compressing 6-8 hours into 60-80 seconds of stillness while crouched are ours; (3) 'living' windows are shown as blinds raised over a dim room (the page gives no visual), and about a third of vacant windows turn out to be living ones because the page's own warning says windows are not exits; (4) the luminous ceiling, walkway heights (8 m, 16 m), the bridge, the fixed corridor annex behind one wall and the two alternating ground doorways are our layout for the page's corridors, stairwells and walkways; (5) the arrival from Level 25's cabinet comes through this level's entry window and that window is the @origin return; (6) skin-stealers and the 'space station' memory are not represented. QA: the bot climbs back out through the open entry window, which the page names as the way out.
